findings.summary: The caption promises a closing config checklist and error-triage table that the ten pages never reach — the part stops mid-way through session resumption.
findings.evidence: Caption: "ends with the config checklist and error-triage table you actually reach for at 2am. 10 pages, no fluff", but page 10 (the last) ends on the "Early Data Replays" callout; syllabus chapters 9 ("What Encryption Does NOT Hide") and 10 ("Failures, Fixes, and the Field Checklist") have no slides.
findings.fix: Either carry the deck through the metadata-leakage and checklist chapters, or trim the caption to describe only what these ten pages actually deliver (handshakes, certs, chains, hostname verification, SNI, resumption).

findings.summary: The caption promises a closing config checklist and error-triage table that no page in the 10-title deck delivers.
findings.evidence: Caption: "ends with the config checklist and error-triage table you actually reach for at 2am" — but the final pages are "SNI: One IP, Many Sites" and "SNI: One IP, Many Sites (cont.)", and no title anywhere covers configuration or error triage.
findings.fix: Drop that clause and end the caption on what the deck actually closes with, e.g. "...and ends by showing why SNI still leaks every hostname you visit, even on TLS 1.3." (Or add the two missing pages if the checklist and triage table were meant to be in the deck.)

findings.summary: AEAD and MAC are introduced as load-bearing terms with no expansion or definition anywhere in the part.
findings.evidence: Page 2: "Each record independently MAC'd or AEAD-sealed"; page 4 then relies on them: "AEAD-only: AES-GCM, AES-CCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305" and "No encrypt-then-MAC vs MAC-then-encrypt footgun".
findings.fix: Expand both at first use on page 2: "Each record is sealed with an AEAD (authenticated encryption — encrypts and authenticates in one pass), or in older suites encrypted and MAC'd (message authentication code)"; page 4's footgun bullet then reads.

findings.summary: The key-derivation code block is placed before the bullets that introduce its inputs, and `pre_master` is never connected to the ECDHE shared secret the reader was just told both sides computed.
findings.evidence: Code block "master = PRF(pre_master, cli_rnd, srv_rnd)" appears above the bullets "ClientKeyExchange carries the client ephemeral key" / "Both sides now compute the same ECDHE secret" / "Pre-master + both randoms feed the PRF".
findings.fix: Move the code block below those bullets, and add the missing link as a bullet: "That shared ECDHE secret IS the pre-master secret" — so the formula's inputs are all named before the formula appears.

findings.summary: "SCTs" and "CT" are used as bare acronyms one page before Certificate Transparency is explained, and neither is ever spelled out.
findings.evidence: Page 6 sidebox: "SCTs prove CT logging — Chrome rejects certs without". CT is first explained on page 7: "Every public cert must hit append-only CT logs".
findings.fix: Either move that bullet to page 7's "Transparency As Mitigation" block, or expand it in place: "SCTs (Signed Certificate Timestamps) prove the cert was published to a Certificate Transparency (CT) log — Chrome rejects public certs without them (page 7)".

findings.summary: The nginx snippet attached to the ticket-key rotation advice does not show key rotation, only session timeout, leaving the page's actionable claim without a supporting example.
findings.evidence: Bullets say "Rotate in hours, not months, and keep keys in memory"; the snippet is "ssl_session_tickets on; / ssl_session_timeout 1h;  # short-lived / # rotate keys; never back them to disk" — `ssl_session_timeout` caps ticket validity, it does not rotate the ticket key.
findings.fix: Show the rotation surface (`ssl_session_ticket_key` pointing at dated key files, reloaded on a timer) or state plainly that nginx has no built-in rotation and the timeout only caps ticket lifetime.

findings.summary: #opensource is unrelated to the handbook's subject matter.
findings.evidence: Hashtags include "#opensource" alongside "#https", "#tls", "#tls13", "#networksecurity"; nothing in the caption or the 10 titles concerns open-source software, licensing, or projects.
findings.fix: Replace "#opensource" with a topic-relevant tag such as "#ssl" or "#infosec".

findings.summary: "mTLS" is used on the opening page but not defined until page 8.
findings.evidence: Page 1: "Client only proves itself under mTLS"; page 8 sidebox "mTLS Flips It" is the first explanation: "Server sends a CertificateRequest / Client presents its own certificate".
findings.fix: Gloss it at first use: "Client only proves itself under mTLS — mutual TLS, where both sides present certs (page 8)".

findings.summary: The hybrid-crypto block never names the asymmetric/symmetric split it is built on, leaving "asymmetric math" undefined when it reappears on page 10.
findings.evidence: Page 2 heading "Hybrid Crypto Cost" with rows "Key agreement | RSA / ECDHE | slow, once" and "Bulk data | AES / ChaCha20 | near-free" — neither "asymmetric" nor "symmetric" appears; page 10 then says "A full handshake costs round trips plus asymmetric math".
findings.fix: Label the split explicitly — add a bullet above the table: "Asymmetric crypto (RSA/ECDHE, slow) is used only to agree on keys; symmetric crypto (AES/ChaCha20, fast) carries all bulk data — that's the 'hybrid'."

findings.summary: A closing callout leans on SNI as a significant leak six pages before SNI is defined.
findings.evidence: Page 3 callout: "Everything through ServerHelloDone is in the clear in TLS 1.2 — the certificate and the SNI are both readable on the wire." SNI is first expanded on page 9: "SNI (RFC 6066) puts the hostname in ClientHello".
findings.fix: Gloss SNI where it first appears on page 2's ClientHello bullets — "SNI (the hostname the client is asking for — page 9), ALPN, curves, sig algs" — so the page 3 callout has meaning when it lands.

findings.summary: Chain vocabulary (leaf, intermediate, root) and the claim that the root is omitted are used three pages before the chain is explained.
findings.evidence: Page 3: "Certificate: leaf plus intermediate CAs" / "Chain order matters; root is normally omitted". The chain is only explained on page 6: "Leaf, then intermediates, then a root" and "The root is NOT sent on the wire / It must already be in the client's trust store".
findings.fix: Add a one-line gloss on page 3: "leaf = this server's cert; intermediates chain it up to a root the client already has, which is why the root isn't sent (page 6)".

findings.summary: The page titled "Step by Step" opens at step 3, because steps 1–2 sit on the previous page under the previous chapter's title.
findings.evidence: Page 3 page_title is "The TLS 1.2 Handshake, Step by Step" and its first heading is "The Server's Half" (Certificate = step 3); ClientHello and ServerHello are on page 2, titled "What HTTPS Actually Is (cont.)".
findings.fix: Either move the "Hello Exchange" block and its flow diagram onto page 3, or open page 3 with a one-line recap — "steps 1–2 (ClientHello, ServerHello) on the previous page" — so a reader navigating by title isn't dropped mid-sequence.
